stories.headline: Stripe Agrees to Buy OpenRouter for More Than $7 Billion, Five Times Its May Valuation
stories.key_takeaway: Stripe has reportedly agreed to pay more than $7 billion for OpenRouter, 5.4x the model router's $1.3 billion valuation 90 days earlier, buying not a model but the metering-and-routing layer through which roughly 100 trillion tokens of monthly inference traffic already flows.

pull_quote.text: Running inference at scale is fundamentally a multi-model problem. The era of picking a single model is over.

stories.article_excerpt: Ninety days ago, OpenRouter was a 30-person startup that had just talked investors into a $1.3 billion valuation.

stories.headline: Nvidia Guarantees $105 Billion in Credit for OpenAI's Ohio Data Center
stories.key_takeaway: Nvidia has agreed to guarantee up to $105 billion in lease and power obligations for OpenAI's 8-gigawatt Ohio data center and taken a $1.5 billion equity stake in its landlord, deepening the circularity concerns shadowing the AI buildout.

pull_quote.text: Is this circular financing? No. OpenAI will pay the lease.

stories.article_excerpt: Nvidia spent Monday doing something chipmakers do not normally do: it co-signed a data center.

stories.headline: AI Video Startup Higgsfield Raises $400 Million at a $5.4 Billion Valuation as Enterprise Revenue Takes Over
stories.key_takeaway: Higgsfield's $400M raise at $5.4B is priced off a 35-fold revenue jump to $700M annualized, but the real story is that business customers flipped from under a quarter of sales in January to the majority today.

pull_quote.text: Every business needs visual content, but creating it at the quality, speed and scale companies demand remains complex and expensive.

stories.article_excerpt: Higgsfield, the AI video and image generation startup founded by former Snap executive Alex Mashrabov, said Monday it has raised $400 million.

stories.headline: Anthropic Reports Its First Profitable Quarter, Splitting the AI Industry Into Two Business Models
stories.key_takeaway: Anthropic told investors it cleared $11.5B in Q2 revenue with positive adjusted operating income, the first claimed profitable quarter by a frontier AI lab, but the figures are preliminary, unaudited, and disputed by critics who say a temporary compute discount created them.

pull_quote.text: We could be profitable in 2026 if the revenue grows fast enough.

stories.article_excerpt: Anthropic has told investors it booked more than $11.5 billion in revenue in the second quarter and turned positive adjusted operating income.

stories.headline: Unitree Sets an August 19 Shanghai Debut After an IPO Oversubscribed 8,000 Times
stories.key_takeaway: Unitree's record-shattering STAR Market IPO gives the world its first public, liquid price on 'physical AI' — and at 219 times earnings, it prices in years of commercialization the humanoid industry has not yet delivered.

pull_quote.text: Given China's advantages in industrial supply chains and talent, the country's embodied intelligence industry chain may bring a surprise to the world.

stories.article_excerpt: Chinese retail investors asked for roughly 8,288 times the stock on offer. They got odds of 0.0181%.

stories.headline: Z.ai's GLM-5.3 Pushes Agentic Coding Through RL Post-Training — and Surfaces Emergent Cyber Skills
stories.key_takeaway: Z.ai got frontier-adjacent agentic coding gains out of GLM-5.2's unchanged base model purely by scaling RL post-training, and the same run produced vulnerability-discovery skills strong enough that the lab delayed its open-weights release by two weeks.

pull_quote.text: GLM-5.3 is our strongest coding agent so far. It scores more than six times higher on Terminal-Bench 3.0 and ranks #1 among open models on 8 out of 9 benchmarks.

stories.article_excerpt: Z.ai did not train a new model. It kept training the old one — and what came out is now the strongest open-weight coder.

stories.headline: OpenAI Puts GPT-5.6 Sol on Cerebras Silicon, Hitting Roughly 750 Tokens a Second
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI's Cerebras-powered Ultrafast preview runs GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 750 output tokens per second with no loss of intelligence, turning inference speed rather than benchmark score into the frontier labs' next competitive axis.

pull_quote.text: GPT-5.6 Sol on Ultrafast is proof that speed and intelligence are no longer mutually exclusive.

stories.article_excerpt: For three years the deal every AI developer had to accept was simple: you could have the smart model or the fast one. Pick.

stories.headline: Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B Puts a Multimodal Open-Weight Model on a Consumer Laptop
stories.key_takeaway: Alibaba's Apache 2.0-licensed Qwen3.8-27B compresses a natively multimodal, 262K-context dense model into a 17GB 4-bit file that runs on a 24GB consumer GPU, drawing 3 million downloads in its first weekend.

pull_quote.text: The fact that a 17GB file can do all of this stuff on my home machines is a miracle. A year ago this would have been competitive with the best and most expensive of the proprietary models — today it can run on a capable laptop.
pull_quote.role: Independent developer and creator of Datasette

stories.article_excerpt: Alibaba's Qwen team pushed Qwen3.8-27B to Hugging Face on Friday, August 14. By Sunday it had been downloaded millions of times.

stories.headline: Google Switched Off Imagen 4 on Monday. Developers Have to Move to Gemini.
stories.key_takeaway: Google's three stable Imagen 4 endpoints became eligible for shutdown on August 17, 2026, and the recommended replacement uses a different API surface, drops five configuration parameters and costs roughly 68% more per 1,000 images.

pull_quote.text: We're really pushing visual quality forward, as well as the model's ability to follow instructions.
pull_quote.role: Product lead, visual generation models, Google DeepMind

stories.article_excerpt: Google's dedicated image-generation model line ended on Monday. Three stable Imagen 4 endpoints went dark.

stories.headline: OpenAI's 'Computer History' Gives ChatGPT a Memory of Your Desktop — Without the Screenshots
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI's opt-in Computer History logs structured interaction events instead of screenshots, sidestepping Microsoft Recall's visual-archive problem while creating a plaintext, machine-readable record that OpenAI itself warns widens the prompt-injection attack surface.

pull_quote.text: Computer History doesn't rely on screen or audio capture. Instead, it captures interaction events like clicking, typing, app switches, and more, so it can capture memories faster and more efficiently.

stories.article_excerpt: OpenAI has given ChatGPT a working memory of your desktop, and it built the thing by conspicuously avoiding one design choice.

stories.headline: Researchers Fuse Synthetic DNA With a Semiconductor to Build an Ultra-Low-Power In-Memory Computing Device
stories.key_takeaway: Penn State researchers built a memristor pairing silver-doped synthetic DNA with a quasi-2D perovskite semiconductor that switches below 0.1 volts, a promising compute-in-memory demonstration whose endurance and retention remain far short of commercial requirements.

pull_quote.text: Using just the DNA or just perovskite alone did not produce near as robust a result as the combination. It's this combination that enables a very high memory storage density that requires very little power.
pull_quote.role: Postdoctoral researcher and co-corresponding author, Penn State

stories.article_excerpt: A team led by Penn State materials scientists has built a memory device that runs on less than a tenth of a volt.

stories.headline: Notion's Knowledge Board Scores Models on Dollars per Completed Task, Not Benchmarks
stories.key_takeaway: Notion's Knowledge Board grades 15 models on live, anonymized production traffic and shows a 43x cost spread across a 4.7-point quality range, reframing model selection around dollars per completed task rather than capability scores.

pull_quote.text: The right model is not the one that wins the most screenshots. It is the one that lets your system finish more work per dollar without making the expensive mistakes.

data_points.label: Claude Opus 5 resolution rate and cost

stories.article_excerpt: The cheapest model on Notion's new Knowledge Board resolves 95.34% of real knowledge-work tasks for two cents.

stories.headline: Databricks Says a Small Classifier Cut Its Coding-Agent Bill 35% by Picking the Right Model First
stories.key_takeaway: Databricks put a cheap classifier in front of its coding agents to size each task before execution and route it to an appropriately priced model, cutting cost per task 35% internally and 56% on public benchmarks while matching any single frontier model.

pull_quote.text: Opening prompts are rarely precise, since what a developer types first is a symptom or a rough intention rather than a specification, and our router reads that first message and commits.
pull_quote.role: Lead author, Smart Routing in Unity AI Gateway, Databricks

stories.article_excerpt: Databricks' own engineers were doing what most enterprise developers do in 2026: pointing every coding task at the most expensive model.

stories.headline: The Wires Between GPUs Are Becoming a $144 Billion Problem
stories.key_takeaway: Copper's reach collapses to about one meter at 224 Gbps per lane, pushing AI clusters toward co-packaged silicon photonics and turning interconnect into a first-order constraint — and a market some vendor-adjacent forecasts put at $144 billion by 2030.

pull_quote.text: AI factories are a new class of data centers with extreme scale, and networking infrastructure must be reinvented to keep pace.

data_points.label: Power per 1.6T port, CPO vs pluggable

stories.article_excerpt: The most expensive part of a frontier training run is no longer the GPU. It is increasingly the problem of getting data between them.

stories.headline: How Fast Could an AI Economy Actually Grow? A New Model Says the Ceiling Is Physical, Not Cognitive
stories.key_takeaway: A widely circulated input-output model argues a fully automated economy could double in nine months to two years using only today's production methods, with construction and metals — not chips — as the binding constraints, though economists say its fixed-price, fixed-technology assumptions push growth modeling past where it was validated.

pull_quote.text: The standard economic prediction of slow growth is implicitly a prediction that full automation will not happen. That may be right, but it is a claim about technology rather than economics.

data_points.label: Construction share of output, model vs today

stories.article_excerpt: Strip away wages and the scarcity of workers, and ask a narrower question: how fast can a pile of factories, mines and power plants copy itself?

stories.headline: OpenAI Dissolves Its Preparedness Team, Folding Frontier-Risk Work Into Product Groups
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI dissolved its Preparedness team at the end of July and scattered biological and cyber risk evaluation into product-adjacent groups, leaving its Preparedness Framework commitments intact but with no single named owner of the catastrophic-risk picture.

pull_quote.text: But over the past years, safety culture and processes have taken a backseat to shiny products.

stories.article_excerpt: The team whose entire job was to ask whether OpenAI's own models could help someone build a bioweapon no longer exists.

stories.headline: OpenAI Funds 14 Think Tanks to Study the Economy It Is Reshaping
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI is putting $1 million in cash and up to $1 million in model credits behind 14 independent research projects on AI's economic disruption, a real capacity boost for underfunded policy shops that also lets the company seed the agenda with questions it framed first.

pull_quote.text: Democracies need to decide how AI is deployed, and organizations like these can serve as laboratories of democracy that develop new ways to ensure AI's gains reach the many, not just the few.

stories.article_excerpt: OpenAI is writing checks to the people who will grade its homework.

stories.headline: A Trump-Backed Crypto Venture Is Routing Payments to an AI Platform Stocked With Chinese Models
stories.key_takeaway: Reuters found that 43 of the 90 AI models on Hong Kong-based WorldClaw come from Chinese firms the US has restricted, and the platform accepts the Trump family's USD1 stablecoin — an arrangement Reuters stressed is not illegal but which experts say collides with Washington's own China AI posture.

pull_quote.text: As the U.S. government tries to respond to the rise and threat of Chinese AI, it seems hypocritical to go out through WorldClaw to use these tools from China to try and make a bunch of money.
pull_quote.role: Fellow, Georgetown Center for Security and Emerging Technology

data_points.label: Trump family stake in World Liberty
Daily requested tasks on the platform
DeepSeek V4 Flash input token price

stories.article_excerpt: Nearly half the AI models on a Hong Kong platform that accepts the Trump family's stablecoin were built by Chinese companies.

stories.headline: California's AI Bills Move Toward a Vote, and the Preemption Fight Comes With Them
stories.key_takeaway: Twenty-four California AI bills survived the Aug. 13 suspense hearings and now face floor votes before the Aug. 31 adjournment, with industry groups opposing the core measures and a federal preemption campaign already suspending a comparable law in Colorado.

pull_quote.text: It's time for California to take the lead in establishing commonsense safety standards for artificial intelligence, since Washington, DC is unable or unwilling to do so.

stories.article_excerpt: California's legislature spent less than an hour on Aug. 13 deciding the fate of its entire artificial intelligence agenda.
